top.title: Royal Navy orders £142M in minehunting drones from US supplier
top.description: Britain's Royal Navy is investing £142 million ($185 million) in underwater drones to tackle sea mines, but the contract has gone to an American defense supplier. The Ministry of Defence (MoD) says that the UK's ability to protect vital sea routes will be strengthened through the procurement of these Uncrewed Underwater Vehicles (UUVs). These will form part of the Royal Navy's move toward a " Hybrid Navy " comprising a mix of crewed, uncrewed, and autonomous platforms in order to meet future challenges. The UUV selected for the job is the REMUS 620 , built by Huntington Ingalls Industries (HII), the largest military shipbuilding company in the United States. HII has a facility at Portchester, on the south coast of England, but is still a US-owned company. We asked the MoD how the award fits its pledge to prioritize buying British wherever possible, and what share of the contract's value will support UK industry. The contract includes HII's Sea Launcher automated launch and recovery systems and will bring support services previously delivered overseas to the UK. HII says it will support 15 jobs, while the MoD identifies Portchester among the locations benefiting. HII says this is the largest international order in its 25-year history of supplying uncrewed systems. The MoD has previously acquired REMUS 100, REMUS 300, and REMUS 600 vehicles for mine countermeasure operations. The new vehicles will locate sea mines to support clearance operations and help keep shipping routes open. By using drones to comb a body of water for explosive devices, the Royal Navy's crews can be kept a safe distance from any potential immediate threat. Traditionally, this work has been conducted by specialist crewed ships such as the Hunt class or Sandown class , but these are being retired from service in favor of uncrewed systems. The Royal Navy also operates SWEEP , an uncrewed boat towing equipment that mimics a ship's magnetic, acoustic, and electric signatures to trigger mines from a safe distance. The new REMUS underwater vehicles can be sent ahead of other vessels to search beneath the surface, making minehunting operations safer, faster and more flexible, according to the MoD. "This investment strengthens our ability to protect freedom of navigation, which is critical to our security and our economy," said Defence Secretary Wes Streeting MP. Like others in the portfolio, REMUS 620 resembles a naval torpedo. It is capable of operating at depths of 600 meters and has an endurance of up to 110 hours on a single mission. The drones will be integrated with SeeTrack and Neptune software developed by SeeByte in the UK, which is already used by the Royal Navy. In trials announced in October 2025, a REMUS 620 demonstrated launch and recovery using a submerged test fixture replicating a Virginia-class submarine's torpedo tube. The work could enable submarines to deploy and retrieve underwater drones on future missions. ®

top.title: People who opposed Tinubu now work with him — Fashola
top.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has said President Bola Tinubu’s ability to retain former allies and reconcile political opponents demonstrates his capacity to manage Nigeria’s diversity and build consensus. Fashola said politicians who opposed Tinubu in the past had now joined forces with him, describing the president’s ability to bring former adversaries together as evidence of his leadership and capacity to work with others. He spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to why Nigerians should give Tinubu another four years in office. The former minister of works said voters should assess the presidential candidates based on their relationships with people they previously worked with, arguing that the ability to sustain working relationships through difficult periods was an important measure of leadership. “The three main presidential candidates today share one trait in common. They all started as governors. One of them didn’t take office, but he was already a governor-elect, Vice President Atiku Abubakar. Where are all the people who worked with them today? That’s a job reference question for those who want to vote,” Fashola said. He asked why many of those who worked with Tinubu during his time as Lagos governor had remained with him, while political associates of other candidates had moved on. “Where are all the people who worked with these people? Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so out of office when he wasn’t a president. That’s a very good answer to the question,” he said. Fashola said the loyalty of Tinubu’s associates reflected his ability to work with others and manage disagreements without abandoning relationships, adding that such qualities were important for a president leading a country with diverse interests. “It shows an ability to work with others. If you are going to get entrusted with managing Nigeria’s diverse family, you must be able to work in a team, and you don’t just get up and jump away when there is crisis in the fold,” he said. He contrasted Tinubu’s political experience with that of other candidates, saying the president remained in the APC despite internal crises, while others left the parties through which they rose to prominence. “There was crisis in the APC. He didn’t leave the party. The others have left the parties that brought them to prominence,” Fashola said. The former governor further argued that Tinubu had expanded his political alliances by bringing former opponents into his fold, including those who once strongly opposed him. “All the people who opposed Tinubu when he used to be called the last man standing. All of them are now working with him. Not just those who worked with him before; those who oppose him are now working with him,” he said. top.description: Photo by Jay Biggerstaff/NWSL via Getty Images Brittany Mahomes didn’t mince her words about the NFL’s officiating after the Kansas City Chiefs’ Thanksgiving Day defeat. Brittany Mahomes lashes out at NFL officiating The moment that caught Brittany’s attention was an overturned catch by Rashee Rice in the fourth quarter of the Thanksgiving Day defeat. top.title: Poole's 100-game Pompey adventure
top.description: [Shutterstock] [BBC] In the summer of 2023 free agent Regan Poole turned down a higher salary elsewhere in League One to sign for Portsmouth. He did so believing the move to the south coast presented him with the best opportunity of reaching the Championship and furthering his career. Exactly 100 appearances later, he's been proved correct. Just like Poole's entire career trajectory, his time at Portsmouth has had plenty of ups and downs. After an excellent start and an international debut for Wales, he tore his anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee during an FA Cup defeat at Chesterfield. When he returned, Pompey were struggling to adjust to life in the Championship and the transition wasn't straightforward for Poole. Not helped by having to play many games in quick succession following a serious injury. Poole and Pompey improved and maintained their Championship status. Portsmouth spent, by their standards, significant fees on centre-backs Hayden Matthews and Josh Knight. Neither have looked like dislodging Poole. Even this season Poole struggled at the start, affected by injury and then below Benji Arthur and Conor Shaughnessy in the pecking order. He's fought his way back into the side and now looks every inch the Championship centre-back he was hoping to become. Portsmouth fans always appreciate committed players. Fratton Park is a ground where big tackles get a louder cheers than great pieces of skills. Poole puts his body on the line the way the home fans crave to see. He wears his heart on his sleeve, celebrating great tackles and blocks. He's absolutely buzzing after wins and often has a face of thunder after defeats (although he will front up to the media). Likely in a similar way to fans leaving the ground. Supporters also love to go on a journey with a player. Poole has grown and improved with the team in the nearly three and half years he's been here. His journey through football has been fascinating , making his Newport County debut at just 16 before moving to Manchester United and then fighting his way back up through the EFL. He's now going into the final year of his contract and has made it clear he would love to sign a new one . The club retain an option year in his deal so it seems very unlikely he'll be departing anytime soon. I highly doubt John Mousinho and Richard Hughes mentioned the Premier League when trying to sell the club to Poole. It would still require something miraculous for Pompey to reach the top flight imminently. But the fact I'm even mentioning it highlights what an adventure the first 100 Pompey matches have been for Regan Poole. top.title: US Merchant Marine Academy looking to make more history in Division III football playoffs
top.description: They’re sea-sing the day at the United States Merchant Marine Academy. It’s a historic year for the 8-1 Mariners, who will play in the second round of the Division III football playoffs for the first time in Kings Point history. “It’s really a special team and how close-knit they are,” head coach Jameson Croall told The Post. “Really, when times get difficult … we lean on each other and respond to that adversity together.” A U.S. Merchant Marine Academy player runs up field during his team’s 42-14 blowout win over the Coast Guard Academy on Nov. 14, 2026, in the Secretaries’ Cup at Audi Field in Washington, D.C. Matt Kaminsky/ZUMA Press Wire The Mariners face No. 25 Hampden-Sydney on the road Saturday at noon after a first-round bye. The USMMA returns to the playoffs for the first time since 1994, the academy’s only other berth. It’s a unique situation for midshipmen on the team who were slated to begin their term at sea — where they can be deployed anywhere around the globe — right after the regular season ended. Several players are spending their mornings on the academy’s flagship vessel, the Kings Pointer, as an interim solution while they wait for long-term stationing after the playoffs. They come back to land and practice in the evening, ready to work, Croall said. “Their ability to compartmentalize all of those things and be able to focus on what they need to focus on in the moment is really a pretty special quality that I think embodies our team. “We really don’t have many bad practices.” The Mariners have also been sailing to victory thanks to dual-threat junior quarterback Bubba Mustain, who averaged 100 rushing yards per game and threw for 16 touchdowns in nine weeks. “He’s really just a complete player with a team around him that’s fully bought in and able to make plays for him as well.”

Rice, 57, certainly wasn’t pleased with Monmouth’s performance in an 85-45 defeat to North Carolina . But after nearly 500 games as the Hawks’ head coach over 16 seasons, he knows wins and losses come and go. What lingered was bigger than results. top.title: Jared Lloyd named Missouri State football Media Player of the Year
top.description: SPRINGFIELD — The Missouri State Media Player of the Year award has returned. Linebacker Jared "Bird" Lloyd was named the 2026 Media Player of the Year on Tuesday, Nov. 24. The Media Player of the Year award had been given to the top Bears player from 1982-2017 and was revived in 2026. “This means a lot. I really appreciate you guys covering me and I’m very appreciative of you guys just getting my name out there more,” Lloyd said. “You guys reporting on me, doesn’t just help me. It helps my teammates, it helps the university and it helps the football program.” Missouri State football: Bears snag its top in-state recruit in the program's history Entering the final game of the season, Lloyd leads the nation with 127 total tackles. He also ranks No. 1 in tackles per game with 11.55. This is the best season by a Missouri State player since 2016, when Dylan Cole set the mark. This is the third-most tackles in a single Missouri State season since 2004. Lloyd also has two sacks, one forced fumble and three pass deflections. The Daytona Beach, Florida, native will finish his career with more than 275 tackles in his five seasons in Springfield. “Bird will go down in history as one of the most important players in Missouri State football history, shepherding this team into the FBS era. He has been one of the best tacklers in college football in 2026,” the News-Leader's Liam Keating said in a press release. “Instead of competing for individual accolades, he's always been a team-first player. This is what makes him a special player and worthy of the first media-given award in almost a decade.” Lloyd is the seventh linebacker to win the award. Ken Braden (1986), Matt Soraghan (’87), James Turnage (’88), DeLaun Fowler (’94-95), P.J. Jones (’01) and Cole (’15-16) were named winners. Missouri State: How star Kaemyn Bekemeier has mastered the NIL era "There's something satisfying about seeing the fruits of one's labor play out before your very eyes," Collingwood said. "Lloyd made a concerted effort to get leaner and quicker in the offseason, and it's translated into him being the country's most prolific tackler. Between his hard work, matter-of-fact disposition, productivity, and rare five-year allegiance to the same school, Lloyd is certainly deserving of this award." Missouri State (4-7, 3-4 CUSA) will host No. 21 Liberty (10-1, 7-0) at 1 p.m. for senior day on Saturday, Nov. 28. This will be Lloyd’s final game representing the Bears inside Plaster Stadium. top.title: KJ Duff reflects on Rutgers football legacy as his NFL decision looms
top.description: PISCATAWAY – All KJ Duff knew at the time was that he couldn’t finish the rest of the game. Rutgers football’s star wide receiver had reaggravated an injury during the Scarlet Knights ’ game against Michigan that he had suffered the week prior, but even as he walked off the SHI Stadium field the possibility he had played his last snap never crossed his mind. Then came the diagnosis of a high-ankle sprain, followed by surgery that would end his season four games too soon. “It definitely was frustrating,” Duff told USA TODAY-New Jersey this week. “All I really want to do is play football, and then that gets taken away.” Frustrating for Duff. Disappointing for the program. And perhaps more disappointing for a fanbase that, for three seasons, watched Duff develop into one of the best receivers in the program’s history, climbing lists in the record books, filling highlight reels with jaw-dropping catches and cementing a legacy that won’t soon be forgotten. Duff hasn’t officially announced his future – whether he’ll pursue the NFL or return to Rutgers for his final year of eligibility. But Duff is projected as a potential first-round draft pick. He’d become the first Rutgers player to hold that distinction since 2010. Coach Greg Schiano also said after a recent game that if Duff asked him, he’d advise him to pursue the NFL. If Duff makes that choice, Schiano made it clear he’ll miss having him in the program. The reasons why are clear. “I’ve told everybody that comes here, it was a lot of fun while it lasted because our hardest working player was our best player,” Schiano said. “That’s fun when you can point to him as an example. Especially in this era of so many newcomers, like, ‘Look what he’s doing, Try to do that.’” That work paid off. “It feels great to be recognized as that, but it's really about what you put into it,” Duff said. “I go with that mentality of, ‘I want to be great.’ I want to put myself in the best position to be successful.” Duff said his focus now is on getting healthy, which was off to a good start just more than two weeks after surgery. Duff said he was already doing some jogging and his doctors said he’s ahead of schedule in his recovery after initially saying he’d be able to resume football activities in January. “I don't want to rush anything and put myself in a bad position,” Duff said. In eight games this season before getting hurt, Duff had 774 receiving yards on 45 catches with a season-high nine touchdowns. He had at least 100 receiving yards in four of those games. top.title: Carlos Alcaraz claimed to have made a change to his game inspired by Pete Sampras ahead of 2027
top.description: One of the many things that makes Carlos Alcaraz so great is his constant willingness to improve. Time and time again, he has proven himself the best player in the world, having strolled to major titles or beaten his rivals with minimal fuss. Normally, that could encourage complacency, and he would have been forgiven for occasionally succumbing to that notion. However, that has yet to happen. Every time it feels like the 23-year-old simply cannot get any better, he manages it, with his current run of form no different. Carlos Alcaraz spent nearly five months sidelined due to injury this year, but even that has not prevented him from improving a key area of his game, which has now been compared to one of the sport’s greatest-ever players. Carlos Alcaraz discusses his changes to his serve Alcaraz’s serve has been a much-discussed topic for years now. After all, if a weakness had to be selected in the Spaniard’s game, this used to be it, with it more than capable, but far from a lethal weapon. Photo by Darren Carroll/USTA via Getty Images Then, last year, he served his way to US Open glory once again, reaching the final without dropping a set and getting broken just three times en route to the title. Even that was not enough, with Alcaraz reportedly having made further tweaks to this all-important shot. According to Marca , the latest changes are inspired by Pete Sampras, one of the greatest servers in tennis history, with particular focus on his raised foot movement during the motion. Samu Lopez, his coach, added: “We were looking for him to have more balance at the beginning of the movement, and that would help him to be more fluid and that he could push himself upwards.” Then, at a Davis Cup press conference earlier this week, Alcaraz directly addressed these changes, admitting: “Whoever hits harder and closer to the lines is the one who wins. The tighter you play to the lines, the better your chances of getting into an attacking position or even winning the point. 🎙️Carlos on his serve improvements: “Whoever hits harder and closer to the lines is the one who wins. The tighter you play to the lines, the better your chances of getting into an attacking position or even winning the point. “I don't usually look at stats during practice. I do… https://t.co/BK02s8kU8T pic.twitter.com/cT7b0gk1kt — Alcaraz Daily (@alcarazdaily) November 26, 2026 “I don’t usually look at stats during practice. I do look at them after matches, because they matter for the next round. We know how important the serve is. It’s something we’ve improved and put a lot of focus on. “Since the US Open, this is the hardest I’ve worked on my serve. Accuracy was a big part of it, and we’ve worked on it more because I’m not very tall and can’t serve like some other players.” Earlier this year, Alcaraz’s serve was accused of ‘not doing enough damage’ . It’s incredible how he has managed to combat those complaints despite spending so long out injured with a wrist injury.

top.description: Barcelona’s unlikely goal machine is starting to make his case Gabriel Jesus has made an encouraging start to life at Barcelona, scoring five goals in just 376 minutes despite struggling to secure regular playing time. The Brazilian striker arrived at Spotify Camp Nou to take over Robert Lewandowski’s place, but has found opportunities limited by Raphinha’s remarkable form in the centre forward position. While expectations were modest compared with those surrounding Lewandowski, Jesus is beginning to show why Barcelona brought him to the club. His goalscoring return has been particularly impressive considering he has made only 11 appearances and had not completed a full match before the Champions League fixture against Sabah in Baku. Gabriel Jesus scores whenever Flick starts him One of the most striking aspects of Jesus’ Barcelona career so far is his record when selected from the beginning. The striker has scored in all three matches in which Hansi Flick has started him, finding the net against Getafe, Real Betis and Sabah. Gabriel Jesus has scored five goals in very limited time for Barcelona. (Picture credit: Barcelona website) His goal in Baku came from close range , with Jesus reacting quickly to a loose ball inside the penalty area. It was not a spectacular finish, but it still showed the instinctive positioning that has become a feature of his performances. As such, the Brazilian has scored five goals in 376 minutes, which translates to a goal every 76 minutes. Barcelona have discovered a natural finisher Jesus, who signed from Arsenal, has already shown different ways of scoring during his short Barcelona spell, having demonstrated quality in the air, the ability to finish with either foot, a powerful strike and composure when opportunities arrive inside the box. His greatest strength, however, may be his anticipation. Jesus regularly positions himself to react before defenders, allowing him to convert chances that might otherwise disappear. top.description: Real Madrid forward knows he is more likely to win the Ballon d’Or as a number nine As we near the halfway point of the season, it is safe to say that Kylian Mbappe has emerged as one of the best performers in Europe. The Frenchman has continued his goalscoring exploits at Santiago Bernabeu, having racked up as many as 19 goals across all competitions. Mbappe has looked quite fit in doing so as well, as he has played in every single one of Real Madrid’s matches so far, leading the club to believe that the player is at the peak of his physical performance. Mbappe’s bid to win Ballon d’Or Mbappe has embraced the number nine role at Real Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Given the sheer productivity Mbappe has provided to the table at Real Madrid this season, it goes without saying that he will once again be one of the candidates to win the Ballon d’Or next year. Keeping that in mind, El Chiringuito has recently claimed that Mbappe himself is aware of the fact that he has more chances of winning the Ballon d’Or if he continues to operate as a number nine. This comes against the backdrop of earlier allegations against Mbappe that he enjoys operating more as a left-winger. In the months since, Mbappe has now fully embraced the role of a number nine, and this has been quite evident in his performances this season. Although the Frenchman still has the tendency to drift out wide, he has done so far less frequently in recent weeks and his overall combination play with other attackers has improved tenfold. Real Madrid, as a result, have dominated their opponents. Can Mbappe win the Ballon d’Or? Mbappe finished second in the 2026 Ballon d’Or. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Mbappe’s numbers so far this season make it obvious that he will be one of the leading candidates to win the Ballon d’Or next year. However, the Frenchman’s fate will once again depend on whether or not Real Madrid can secure any silverware this season. Los Blancos have not won a single major trophy in two seasons, so breaking that rut could go a long way in boosting Mbappe’s chances of winning his first Ballon d’Or. Fortunately, with Jose Mourinho, Real Madrid now have a seasoned coach who has shown exceptional decision-making skills and has the technical know-how in competitions such as the Champions League. Mbappe, to that end, will play an integral part of Mourinho’s war machine as they look to break Real Madrid’s trophy rut during the second half of the campaign.

top.title: Cam Smith reacts to shooting 64 in Australia despite hitting ‘the worst shot’ he has ever hit as a pro
top.description: Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images Cam Smith vaulted himself back into contention at the Australian PGA Championship on Friday. Smith shot a superb round of 64, one that even featured a bogey. The 33-year-old Australian carded seven birdies and an eagle during his second round at The Lakes on Friday. Cam Smith is now sitting just four shots adrift of the leader, Nicolai von Dellingshausen, with 36 holes left to play. Smith is looking to win his fourth Australian PGA Championship this week, and if he carries on playing like he did on Friday across the weekend, he will have a great chance to do just that. Cam Smith reacts to shooting 64 at the Australian PGA Smith wasn’t entirely happy with his opening round in Australia on Thursday, so he would have been delighted to see such drastic improvements on day two. The former LIV Golf star spoke to reporters after shooting a second-round 64 and responded when asked to give his verdict on his current form. “Yeah, I think so, it’s definitely going to be a different year. I’m excited. I haven’t done the European stuff before, and just starting at home is pretty special,” Smith said. “I got in a bit of a groove and rhythm today, which is what we’ve been looking for. We’ve been searching for that and it finally kind of all came together today.” However, not everything went swimmingly for Smith. The 2022 Open champion hit what he described as probably the worst shot he has ever hit as a professional on the par-three 15th hole. However, after leaving himself a full wedge shot into the green, he holed a 25-foot putt to salvage his par. “That might have been the worst shot I’ve ever hit as a professional,” said Smith. “It wasn’t a shank, but it was close. It definitely kind of kept the momentum going, for sure.” Cam Smith will be hoping to avoid any more card-wrecking shots like the one he hit on the 15th hole on Friday. If he manages to post two rounds in the 60s over the weekend, he may well have a chance of winning the fourth Australian PGA Championship of his career.

nigeria.description: Former Lagos State Governor Babatunde Fashola has said President Bola Tinubu’s ability to retain former allies and reconcile political opponents demonstrates his capacity to manage Nigeria’s diversity and build consensus. Fashola said politicians who opposed Tinubu in the past had now joined forces with him, describing the president’s ability to bring former adversaries together as evidence of his leadership and capacity to work with others. He spoke in an interview with ARISE News while responding to why Nigerians should give Tinubu another four years in office. The former minister of works said voters should assess the presidential candidates based on their relationships with people they previously worked with, arguing that the ability to sustain working relationships through difficult periods was an important measure of leadership. “The three main presidential candidates today share one trait in common. Why is it only President Tinubu that has all those who worked with him still with him? And they were with him for 16 years or so out of office when he wasn’t a president. That’s a very good answer to the question,” he said. Fashola said the loyalty of Tinubu’s associates reflected his ability to work with others and manage disagreements without abandoning relationships, adding that such qualities were important for a president leading a country with diverse interests. “It shows an ability to work with others. The ace singer said frustration over impunity had made calls for severe punishment understandable, while stressing that allegations of rigging must be proven. “You know when a situation gets to a certain point, like right now we’re like on a very mountainous keg of gunpowder right now. Desperate times make you make some kind of statements. This statement sounds correct. It should be like that, actually.” He said the slogan reflected a demand for stronger consequences for election rigging. “If you rig, the punishments should be very severe to deter people from rigging.” 2Baba added: “So the statement itself is rig or die. I don’t see anything that’s wrong with it. It’s like saying embezzle money and die. Na death penalty for China for embezzlement.” He said Nigeria needed serious deterrence for crimes, including kidnapping, and that people were frustrated by what he described as a lack of consequences. “We’re in a stage where we need, we need serious deterrence, anybody who kidnaps is supposed to face serious consequences. “Because it’s getting too much, and people are just getting away with everything. nigeria.title: Nvidia: Women Raise Concerns Over Jensen Huang’s Return
nigeria.description: News of Jensen Huang’s shocking return to Nvidia had barely landed when President Donald Trump posted an AI-generated image of the Nvidia cofounder holding up a red bra, surrounded by security personnel whisking him offstage, blood streaked across his face. The image was based on a real photo taken in 2024 when Trump survived an assassination attempt during a campaign rally in Butler, Pennsylvania, and implied that Huang, too, had survived a bid to take him out. For many women, though, the image spoke insultingly to longstanding frustrations about sexism, double standards and a lack of accountability for men in power — across politics and business. Meanwhile, many “tech bros” rushed to Huang’s defense over the past couple of weeks. Billionaire Elon Musk was among many people who signed a petition calling for Huang’s reinstatement. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang (R) speaks alongside US President Donald Trump about investing in America, at the White House in Washington, DC, on April 30, 2025. Photo by JIM WATSON / AFP Venture capitalist Jason Calacanis described Huang as a “hero” and downplayed the scandal that led to Huang’s resignation as less important than the United States winning the AI race against China. “They’re standing up for the idea that certain men can do whatever they want,” Cleo Capital Managing Director Sarah Kunst told AFP. Part of the problem might be “hero worship,” she said. It also reflects the tech industry’s mythology around “founder mode” — the belief that companies thrive when founders stay hands-on rather than cede control to executives. Huang resigned on November 12 from Nvidia, the company he cofounded and has led for more than three decades, amid allegations that he had multiple extramarital affairs, including one with a woman that US officials suspect was working for Chinese intelligence, triggering national security concerns. nigeria.title: Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat
nigeria.description: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that he had seen sufficient information that Nvidia’s Jensen Huang was not a security threat, while touting his administration’s intervention to save the scandal-plagued CEO’s job as “a great thing” for the world. “I think he’s absolutely fine,” Trump told reporters at his Mar-a-Lago estate. Asked by AFP how he could be sure when the Justice Department would not confirm it had conducted a thorough investigation into Huang, Trump said his belief was based on “information I have, which is a lot of information.” Huang, a key figure in the AI revolution, was forced to resign earlier this month after revelations that he had an affair with a business executive who reportedly has ties to Chinese intelligence and whose company may have helped China obtain advanced chips in violation of US export controls. His sudden resignation saw the stock price of Nvidia plummet, before a shock decision by the board to reinstate him saw a partial rebound. Trump revealed that he and other officials in his administration have worked behind the scenes to push for Huang to be reinstated, in a highly unusual intervention by the government into a top company’s decision making. “I just thought, I saw that what was happening with the company, what was happening with the stock, and I think it’s a great thing that he’s going back,” Trump said Thursday. “So I really… think I did a great thing for our country and even for the world,” Trump said of the effort to back Huang. Asked if he had spoken with Huang since his reinstatement was announced, Trump said no, but then later said: “When I did speak to him, he is so happy to be going back. He calls it his second term.” He also praised Huang’s wife as “phenomenal.” The post Trump insists Nvidia CEO not a security threat appeared first on Vanguard News .

nigeria.title: CeBIH, NIMC to explore digital identity for financial inclusion, growth
nigeria.description: By Babajide Komolafe The Committee of e-Business Industry Heads (CeBIH) and the National Identity Management Commission (NIMC) are set to explore how digital identity can drive financial inclusion, trust and economic growth at the 2026 CeBIH Annual Conference scheduled for December 1 and 2 in Lagos. The conference, themed “Digital Identity: A Catalyst for Financial Inclusion, Trust and Growth,” will bring together policymakers, regulators, financial services leaders and technology innovators to examine the role of identity infrastructure in Nigeria’s digital financial ecosystem. Speaking at a press conference on the theme of the conference, Chairman of CeBIH, Mrs. Abidemi Asunmo, said the future of financial services and the broader digital economy depended significantly on reliable, secure and accessible digital identity infrastructure. “A trusted digital identity ecosystem has implications far beyond registration and identification. It can help address some of the structural barriers to financial inclusion.’’ Gbolahan Oluwatobiloba, Lagos State Coordinator, NIMC, said identity was the foundation of economic development, security and trust. “Identity is the foundation of everything, not just the financial sector, the security sector or the identity ecosystem. When you remove identity, your security will be affected, because how do you secure people you don’t know?” he said. Vice Chairman of CeBIH and Chairman of the Conference Planning Committee, Abednigo Ugwueke, said participants would examine how trusted digital identity could improve customer onboarding, strengthen Know Your Customer processes, enhance identity verification, reduce fraud and expand access to financial services. The conference is expected to feature key government and industry personalities, including NIMC Director-General, Engr. Abisoye Coker-Odusote; Executive Chairman of the Nigeria Revenue Service, Dr. Zach Adedeji; National Commissioner and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigeria Data Protection Commission, Dr. Vincent Olatunji; and Comptroller-General of the Nigeria Immigration Service, Kemi Nanna Nandap. Kayode Olubiyi, Head of Digital Payments, UBA, representing the CeBIH Advisory Council, said customers increasingly prioritised security and trust in banking. nigeria.description: By Ch ioma Obinna & Juliet Umeh Stakeholders, yesterday, called for stronger collaboration among government, the media, private sector and communities to address challenges threatening child survival, education and development in Nigeria. The stakeholders include the United Nations Children’s Fund, UNICEF, Nigerian Guild of Editors, NGE, Lagos State Government and Airtel Nigeria made the call at the 2026 World Children’s Day High-Level Media Symposium themed: ‘Every Child Alive, Thriving and Learning: A Shared Responsibility’ in Lagos. Speaking at the event organised by UNICEF Nigeria in partnership with the NGE and Diamond Awards for Media Excellence, DAME, President of the NGE, Mr. Eze Anaba, said the responsibility of ensuring that Nigerian children survived, received quality education and realised their potential rested on all stakeholders, not government alone. Anaba cited a UNICEF report indicating that 18.3 million Nigerian children were out of school, describing the figure as alarming and calling for urgent collective action. “In a country of over 200 million people, 18 million-plus of that population is on the streets, not going to school. It’s not only alarming; it’s a collective responsibility,” he said. He challenged media organisations, private sector players, community leaders and parents to examine their contributions towards addressing the problem. “Have we reminded the government? Community leaders, have they done their part? Has the media done enough? The private sector, has it done enough?” he asked. Anaba urged stakeholders to develop an action plan with specific commitments, stressing that annual commemorations must translate into measurable improvements in children’s lives. Earlier, UNICEF Chief of Communication, Advocacy and Partnership, Ms. Lone Hvass, said: “Survival, education and learning are deeply interconnected. A child who is out of school is denied much more than education. He or she is denied opportunities for protection, participation and the possibility of realising their full potential. “The media does much more than report on children’s issues. Media helps determine which issues receive public attention, which voices are heard, which assumptions are challenged, and which movements are followed through,” Hvass said. She urged journalists to move beyond episodic coverage and headlines to sustained reporting that connects individual experiences with systemic challenges, provides evidence and exposes gaps in policy implementation. entertainment.title: M.Inc PR Joins Industry Stakeholders to Explore Africa’s Credit Economy at ACE 2026
entertainment.description: A cross section of industry leaders and stakeholders during the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo 2026 held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. What will it take to make credit more accessible to African businesses and individuals? At the fourth edition of Africa Credit Expo (ACE) 202 6, stakeholders across financial services, technology, policy, investment and entrepreneurship examined the role of reliable credit information, financial inclusion and collaboration in expanding access to capital. Powered by CreditRegistry and supported by Afreximbank , the Expo was held on Friday, 13 November 2026, at the J. F. Ade Ajayi Main Auditorium, University of Lagos. Themed “Reimagining Africa’s Credit Economy: Unlocking Capital, Trust and Opportunity,” the event provided a platform for conversations on the systems, innovations and partnerships shaping the future of credit across the continent. Building Trust and Expanding Access to Capital Discussions at the Expo explored the role of credible credit information in building trust between lenders and borrowers. Reliable data enables financial institutions to assess risk more effectively and make informed lending decisions, while individuals and businesses with established credit histories are better positioned to demonstrate their credit worthiness. The conversations also considered the financing constraints facing micro, small and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). Despite their contribution to employment and economic activity, many small businesses continue to encounter barriers to affordable financing. Improving access to relevant financial products and strengthening credit information systems remain important to addressing these gaps. Technology, Financial Inclusion and the Next Generation Digital innovation and data intelligence featured prominently in discussions about the future of credit. Alternative credit assessment approaches have the potential to broaden access for individuals and businesses with limited formal credit histories. However, the expansion of digital financial services must be accompanied by responsible lending practices, consumer protection and transparency. The Expo also placed attention on young people through student-focused sessions and discussions on financial literacy. These conversations connected access to credit with the need for individuals to understand financial management, borrowing and long-term wealth creation. This focus reflects the February 2026 memorandum of understanding between CreditRegistry and the University of Lagos, through its Entrepreneurship and Skills Development Centre (ESDC), to integrate the Africa Consumer Credit Academy (ACCA) curriculum into the Centre’s programmes. The initiative is intended to strengthen financial literacy through learning opportunities, mentorship, certification and engagement with industry. entertainment.title: As Nigeria Rethinks Teacher Education, Tunji Olowolafe Makes a Case for Better-Prepared Educators
entertainment.description: What makes a good teacher? Beyond knowing a subject, a good teacher can understand students, inspire confidence, and help young people discover what they are capable of becoming. It was this broader responsibility of educators that Dr. Tunji Olowolafe explored while delivering the 2026 Convocation Lecture at the Sikiru Adetona College of Education, Science and Technology (SACOETEC), Omu-Ajose, Ogun State. Speaking on Monday, 23 November 2026, on the theme “The Dual-Mandate NCE-Degree Programme: Prospects, Challenges and the Future of Teacher Education in Nigeria,” he described the programme as an important opportunity to reposition teacher education. For decades, Colleges of Education depended on university affiliations to award Bachelor’s degrees, despite many possessing the academic capacity to run such programmes. The Federal Colleges of Education Act 2023 changed this, empowering eligible institutions to award degrees independently. Under the Dual-Mandate programme, students can complete three years of NCE training and proceed to another two years for a Bachelor’s degree in Education. Dr. Olowolafe explained that combining practical teaching skills with deeper academic knowledge would produce better-prepared educators. However, he cautioned that institutional autonomy must be supported by sustained funding, improved curricula and professional development. With Nigeria facing an estimated shortage of one million teachers, he also called for greater integration of vocational education, artificial intelligence and digital skills into learning. “AI can explain a quadratic equation at midnight, but it cannot offer the steady, empathetic guidance of a caring adult,” he said, emphasizing that artificial intelligence must complement, not replace, the human qualities of effective teaching. During the lecture, Dr. Olowolafe announced that the Tunji Olowolafe Foundation would establish a fully equipped, solar-powered Gbemisola Olowolafe Memorial ICT Centre (GOMTECH) with high-speed internet connectivity at SACOETEC. The Foundation is also committed to recognising academic excellence and outstanding teaching at the College. This includes recognising the College’s first-class degree graduates and NCE distinction holders, alongside the overall best NCE and degree graduates. Lecturers, selected based on student ratings, will also be honoured for their teaching contributions. The initiative builds on the Foundation’s existing investment in education, including Project Digi-Teach at Ekiti State University and GOMTECH in Are-Ekiti. For Dr. Olowolafe, the commitment to educators is also deeply personal. His mother was a teacher, his elder sister taught for years at Baptist Academy, Lagos, and his late wife, Gbemisola Olowolafe, was a lifelong educator. He recalled the influence of teachers who shaped his own experience, particularly Mr. Soewu of Methodist Boys’ High School , whose patience helped students understand difficult concepts without humiliation. Then you probably remember that voice. Deep, commanding and unmistakable, it often came with his signature red cap, traditional Igbo attire and a generous helping of proverbs. The actor was just as memorable away from the screen, where his sharp wit, outspoken nature and candid opinions made him a fascinating personality in interviews. He was never one to shy away from saying exactly what he thought, and that straightforwardness became another part of what audiences remembered about him. For generations of Nollywood viewers, Pete Edochie was the actor they could recognise before he had even finished his first sentence. He became one of Nigerian cinema’s most familiar faces, often playing kings, chiefs, fathers and respected elders. His breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart , a performance that helped establish him as one of Nollywood’s most respected actors. The veteran actor passed away in Enugu yesterday, on Wednesday, 25 November 2026, at the age of 79, following a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Born in Zaria and originally from Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Edochie began his career in broadcasting in 1967, eventually rising to become Deputy Managing Director of the Anambra Broadcasting Service. He went on to feature in hundreds of films, including Igodo , The Egg of Life and Lionheart . His performance was so transformative that, for generations of viewers, Edochie and Okonkwo became inseparable. In fashion, the conversation often begins with style, but it rarely ends there. Quality, affordability, accessibility and the story behind what we wear are increasingly becoming part of how consumers make their choices. For Alero Ebigbeyi, these are not just considerations; they are the principles shaping her latest venture, HÉYCH. entertainment.description: Nollywood icon Pete Edochie, MON, who passed away at the age of 79 in Enugu. Photo Credit: Pete Edochie/Instagram Nollywood and the wider African entertainment community are mourning the loss of one of their most respected screen icons, Pete Edochie , MON, who passed away on Wednesday, 25 November 2026,at the age of 79. According to an official statement released on behalf of the family by his eldest son, Leo Pete Edochie , the veteran actor and retired broadcaster departed this life at 12:30 a.m. in Enugu, Nigeria, following a protracted battle with prostate cancer. Born on 7 March 1947 in Zaria, Kaduna State, and hailing from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje in Anambra State, Pete Edochie began his career in broadcasting long before becoming a household name on television and cinema screens. At age 20, in 1967, he joined the Eastern Nigeria Broadcasting Service (ENBS)—later the Anambra Broadcasting Service (ABS)—rising steadily through the ranks to serve as Director of Programmes and Deputy Managing Director. His defining breakthrough came in 1987 when he portrayed the fierce, tragic hero Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority’s (NTA) acclaimed television adaptation of Chinua Achebe ‘s Things Fall Apart. His commanding presence and deep, resonant voice earned him international recognition—including a dedicated delegation interview from the BBC—and cemented his place in Nigerian television history. Over a screen career spanning nearly four decades, Pete Edochie became synonymous with authority,traditional wisdom, and unforgettable Igbo proverbs. Whether playing stern monarchs, principled elders, or complex patriarchs, he delivered every line with unmistakable gravitas. His extensive filmography includes standout appearances in classics and modern hits alike, such as Things Fall Apart (1987), Igodo (1999), Egg of Life (2003), Oracle (2003), Billionaires Club (2003), End of Money (2005), Lionheart (2018)—where he starred as Chief Ernest Obiagu alongside Genevieve Nnaji—Unroyal (2020), and Foreigner’s God (2022). In recognition of his immense contributions to Nigerian arts and culture, he was conferred with the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON) in 2003 by former President Olusegun Obasanjo,alongside the Africa Magic Viewers’ Choice Awards (AMVCA) Industry Merit Award and lifetime achievement honours from the Africa Film Academy and the African Film Festival (TAFF). sports.title: Poole's 100-game Pompey adventure
sports.description: [Shutterstock] [BBC] In the summer of 2023 free agent Regan Poole turned down a higher salary elsewhere in League One to sign for Portsmouth. He did so believing the move to the south coast presented him with the best opportunity of reaching the Championship and furthering his career. Exactly 100 appearances later, he's been proved correct. Just like Poole's entire career trajectory, his time at Portsmouth has had plenty of ups and downs. After an excellent start and an international debut for Wales, he tore his anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee during an FA Cup defeat at Chesterfield. When he returned, Pompey were struggling to adjust to life in the Championship and the transition wasn't straightforward for Poole. Not helped by having to play many games in quick succession following a serious injury. Poole and Pompey improved and maintained their Championship status. Portsmouth spent, by their standards, significant fees on centre-backs Hayden Matthews and Josh Knight. Neither have looked like dislodging Poole. Even this season Poole struggled at the start, affected by injury and then below Benji Arthur and Conor Shaughnessy in the pecking order. He's fought his way back into the side and now looks every inch the Championship centre-back he was hoping to become. Portsmouth fans always appreciate committed players. Fratton Park is a ground where big tackles get a louder cheers than great pieces of skills. Poole puts his body on the line the way the home fans crave to see. He wears his heart on his sleeve, celebrating great tackles and blocks. He's absolutely buzzing after wins and often has a face of thunder after defeats (although he will front up to the media). Likely in a similar way to fans leaving the ground. Supporters also love to go on a journey with a player. Poole has grown and improved with the team in the nearly three and half years he's been here. His journey through football has been fascinating , making his Newport County debut at just 16 before moving to Manchester United and then fighting his way back up through the EFL. He's now going into the final year of his contract and has made it clear he would love to sign a new one . The club retain an option year in his deal so it seems very unlikely he'll be departing anytime soon. I highly doubt John Mousinho and Richard Hughes mentioned the Premier League when trying to sell the club to Poole. It would still require something miraculous for Pompey to reach the top flight imminently. But the fact I'm even mentioning it highlights what an adventure the first 100 Pompey matches have been for Regan Poole. sports.description: CHAPEL HILL — The emotions didn’t fully hit King Rice until he returned to the visiting locker room at the Smith Center following a 40-point loss to his alma mater. Rice, 57, certainly wasn’t pleased with Monmouth’s performance in an 85-45 defeat to North Carolina . But after nearly 500 games as the Hawks’ head coach over 16 seasons, he knows wins and losses come and go. What lingered was bigger than results. More than 40 years of memories and relationships came flooding back when Rice saw who was waiting for him after the game. So were former Tar Heels assistant coaches Phil Ford and Dave Hanners. Dave Blaha, a former walk-on who often gave Rice rides home to upstate New York during their playing days, was there too. Rice hadn’t seen Blaha since the 1990s. “That’s when it got emotional for me,” Rice said during a 20-minute conversation with The Fayetteville Observer. “Because I didn’t play with Kenny. Obviously, Coach Ford coached me and helped me grow up a whole bunch. But then Coach Hanners came in there and said, ‘Listen to this guy. He cares about y’all, he loves y’all. I know he yells and uses curse words sometimes, but he’s trying to get y’all to do the right things. It’s all from the right place.’ ” It was a special moment because, as Rice mentioned, "those guys are Carolina men and they came to support me" at the Smith Center. “They know I don’t like losing like that. They know that crushed everything in my being, but you got to be a man, you got to stand up. This isn’t the first time I’ve gotten my butt kicked, it’s not going to be the last time I get my butt kicked," Rice said. “But, as a man, you got to stand up. Your friends are still there for you. Even though I didn’t play with those guys, they came to support and that’s where my kids can learn the most from. It’s bigger than basketball. sports.title: Jared Lloyd named Missouri State football Media Player of the Year
sports.description: SPRINGFIELD — The Missouri State Media Player of the Year award has returned. Linebacker Jared "Bird" Lloyd was named the 2026 Media Player of the Year on Tuesday, Nov. 24. The Media Player of the Year award had been given to the top Bears player from 1982-2017 and was revived in 2026. “This means a lot. I really appreciate you guys covering me and I’m very appreciative of you guys just getting my name out there more,” Lloyd said. “You guys reporting on me, doesn’t just help me. It helps my teammates, it helps the university and it helps the football program.” Missouri State football: Bears snag its top in-state recruit in the program's history Entering the final game of the season, Lloyd leads the nation with 127 total tackles. He also ranks No. 1 in tackles per game with 11.55. This is the best season by a Missouri State player since 2016, when Dylan Cole set the mark. This is the third-most tackles in a single Missouri State season since 2004. Lloyd also has two sacks, one forced fumble and three pass deflections. The Daytona Beach, Florida, native will finish his career with more than 275 tackles in his five seasons in Springfield. “Bird will go down in history as one of the most important players in Missouri State football history, shepherding this team into the FBS era. He has been one of the best tacklers in college football in 2026,” the News-Leader's Liam Keating said in a press release. “Instead of competing for individual accolades, he's always been a team-first player. This is what makes him a special player and worthy of the first media-given award in almost a decade.” Lloyd is the seventh linebacker to win the award. Ken Braden (1986), Matt Soraghan (’87), James Turnage (’88), DeLaun Fowler (’94-95), P.J. Jones (’01) and Cole (’15-16) were named winners. Missouri State: How star Kaemyn Bekemeier has mastered the NIL era "There's something satisfying about seeing the fruits of one's labor play out before your very eyes," Collingwood said. "Lloyd made a concerted effort to get leaner and quicker in the offseason, and it's translated into him being the country's most prolific tackler. Missouri State (4-7, 3-4 CUSA) will host No. 21 Liberty (10-1, 7-0) at 1 p.m. for senior day on Saturday, Nov. 28. This will be Lloyd’s final game representing the Bears inside Plaster Stadium. sports.title: KJ Duff reflects on Rutgers football legacy as his NFL decision looms
sports.description: PISCATAWAY – All KJ Duff knew at the time was that he couldn’t finish the rest of the game. Rutgers football’s star wide receiver had reaggravated an injury during the Scarlet Knights ’ game against Michigan that he had suffered the week prior, but even as he walked off the SHI Stadium field the possibility he had played his last snap never crossed his mind. Then came the diagnosis of a high-ankle sprain, followed by surgery that would end his season four games too soon. “It definitely was frustrating,” Duff told USA TODAY-New Jersey this week. “All I really want to do is play football, and then that gets taken away.” Frustrating for Duff. Disappointing for the program. And perhaps more disappointing for a fanbase that, for three seasons, watched Duff develop into one of the best receivers in the program’s history, climbing lists in the record books, filling highlight reels with jaw-dropping catches and cementing a legacy that won’t soon be forgotten. Duff hasn’t officially announced his future – whether he’ll pursue the NFL or return to Rutgers for his final year of eligibility. But Duff is projected as a potential first-round draft pick. He’d become the first Rutgers player to hold that distinction since 2010. Coach Greg Schiano also said after a recent game that if Duff asked him, he’d advise him to pursue the NFL. If Duff makes that choice, Schiano made it clear he’ll miss having him in the program. The reasons why are clear. “I’ve told everybody that comes here, it was a lot of fun while it lasted because our hardest working player was our best player,” Schiano said. “That’s fun when you can point to him as an example. Especially in this era of so many newcomers, like, ‘Look what he’s doing, Try to do that.’” That work paid off. “It feels great to be recognized as that, but it's really about what you put into it,” Duff said. “I go with that mentality of, ‘I want to be great.’ I want to put myself in the best position to be successful.” Duff said his focus now is on getting healthy, which was off to a good start just more than two weeks after surgery. Duff said he was already doing some jogging and his doctors said he’s ahead of schedule in his recovery after initially saying he’d be able to resume football activities in January. “I don't want to rush anything and put myself in a bad position,” Duff said. sports.title: Carlos Alcaraz claimed to have made a change to his game inspired by Pete Sampras ahead of 2027
sports.description: One of the many things that makes Carlos Alcaraz so great is his constant willingness to improve. Time and time again, he has proven himself the best player in the world, having strolled to major titles or beaten his rivals with minimal fuss. Normally, that could encourage complacency, and he would have been forgiven for occasionally succumbing to that notion. However, that has yet to happen. Every time it feels like the 23-year-old simply cannot get any better, he manages it, with his current run of form no different. Carlos Alcaraz spent nearly five months sidelined due to injury this year, but even that has not prevented him from improving a key area of his game, which has now been compared to one of the sport’s greatest-ever players. Carlos Alcaraz discusses his changes to his serve Alcaraz’s serve has been a much-discussed topic for years now. After all, if a weakness had to be selected in the Spaniard’s game, this used to be it, with it more than capable, but far from a lethal weapon. Photo by Darren Carroll/USTA via Getty Images Then, last year, he served his way to US Open glory once again, reaching the final without dropping a set and getting broken just three times en route to the title. Even that was not enough, with Alcaraz reportedly having made further tweaks to this all-important shot. According to Marca , the latest changes are inspired by Pete Sampras, one of the greatest servers in tennis history, with particular focus on his raised foot movement during the motion. Samu Lopez, his coach, added: “We were looking for him to have more balance at the beginning of the movement, and that would help him to be more fluid and that he could push himself upwards.” Then, at a Davis Cup press conference earlier this week, Alcaraz directly addressed these changes, admitting: “Whoever hits harder and closer to the lines is the one who wins. The tighter you play to the lines, the better your chances of getting into an attacking position or even winning the point. 🎙️Carlos on his serve improvements: “Whoever hits harder and closer to the lines is the one who wins. The tighter you play to the lines, the better your chances of getting into an attacking position or even winning the point. “I don't usually look at stats during practice. I do… https://t.co/BK02s8kU8T pic.twitter.com/cT7b0gk1kt — Alcaraz Daily (@alcarazdaily) November 26, 2026 “I don’t usually look at stats during practice. I do look at them after matches, because they matter for the next round. We know how important the serve is. It’s something we’ve improved and put a lot of focus on. “Since the US Open, this is the hardest I’ve worked on my serve. Accuracy was a big part of it, and we’ve worked on it more because I’m not very tall and can’t serve like some other players.” Earlier this year, Alcaraz’s serve was accused of ‘not doing enough damage’ . Mbappe has looked quite fit in doing so as well, as he has played in every single one of Real Madrid’s matches so far, leading the club to believe that the player is at the peak of his physical performance. Mbappe’s bid to win Ballon d’Or Mbappe has embraced the number nine role at Real Madrid. (Photo by Florencia Tan Jun/Getty Images) Given the sheer productivity Mbappe has provided to the table at Real Madrid this season, it goes without saying that he will once again be one of the candidates to win the Ballon d’Or next year. Keeping that in mind, El Chiringuito has recently claimed that Mbappe himself is aware of the fact that he has more chances of winning the Ballon d’Or if he continues to operate as a number nine. This comes against the backdrop of earlier allegations against Mbappe that he enjoys operating more as a left-winger. In the months since, Mbappe has now fully embraced the role of a number nine, and this has been quite evident in his performances this season. Although the Frenchman still has the tendency to drift out wide, he has done so far less frequently in recent weeks and his overall combination play with other attackers has improved tenfold. sports.description: Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images Cam Smith vaulted himself back into contention at the Australian PGA Championship on Friday. Smith shot a superb round of 64, one that even featured a bogey. The 33-year-old Australian carded seven birdies and an eagle during his second round at The Lakes on Friday. Cam Smith is now sitting just four shots adrift of the leader, Nicolai von Dellingshausen, with 36 holes left to play. Smith is looking to win his fourth Australian PGA Championship this week, and if he carries on playing like he did on Friday across the weekend, he will have a great chance to do just that. Cam Smith reacts to shooting 64 at the Australian PGA Smith wasn’t entirely happy with his opening round in Australia on Thursday, so he would have been delighted to see such drastic improvements on day two. The former LIV Golf star spoke to reporters after shooting a second-round 64 and responded when asked to give his verdict on his current form. “Yeah, I think so, it’s definitely going to be a different year. I’m excited. I haven’t done the European stuff before, and just starting at home is pretty special,” Smith said. “I got in a bit of a groove and rhythm today, which is what we’ve been looking for. We’ve been searching for that and it finally kind of all came together today.” However, not everything went swimmingly for Smith. The 2022 Open champion hit what he described as probably the worst shot he has ever hit as a professional on the par-three 15th hole. However, after leaving himself a full wedge shot into the green, he holed a 25-foot putt to salvage his par. “That might have been the worst shot I’ve ever hit as a professional,” said Smith. “It wasn’t a shank, but it was close. It definitely kind of kept the momentum going, for sure.” Cam Smith will be hoping to avoid any more card-wrecking shots like the one he hit on the 15th hole on Friday. If he manages to post two rounds in the 60s over the weekend, he may well have a chance of winning the fourth Australian PGA Championship of his career.

sports.title: Bournemouth equal Nuremberg’s European record
sports.description: Bournemouth equal Nuremberg’s European record Bournemouth are already dreaming on European glory under Marco Rose, and rightly so. After going 1-0 down against Celta Vigo in the UEFA Europa League on Thursday night, having a man sent off and then scoring two goals, the Cherries’ 2-1 victory is their fifth straight win in their maiden European competition. With five wins from five and maximum points, Bournemouth became the first English team, and only the third in history, to win their first five European matches. Only Nuremberg (1961/62) and Ararat Yerevan (1972/73) are the only other teams to record such a feat. It was also their tenth straight victory across all competitions – a record matched only by Real Madrid. Speaking to the BBC Sport after Bournemouth’s latest victory, Rose, formerly of Borussia Mönchengladbach, Borussia Dortmund and RB Leipzig, said: “Dreaming is always allowed. When you participate in a competition like this, you want to achieve the best possible result.” GGFN | Daniel Pinder

sports.title: Eastleigh to keep Hill, Bristow & Bartram in charge
sports.description: Richard Hill is in his fourth spell in charge of Eastleigh, having guided them to promotion to the National League in 2014 [Shutterstock] Eastleigh have confirmed that Richard Hill, Jason Bristow and Vince Bartram will continue to oversee first-team affairs for the foreseeable future. The trio have been in charge of the side on an interim basis since Matt Gray was sacked earlier this month. Former manager Hill had conducted post-match media affairs after Eastleigh's past two games - a 3-1 win at Tamworth and a 3-1 home loss to Yeovil Town. The club had won just one of their final eight matches under Gray and are currently 18th in the National League. The news comes days after owner Stewart Donald confirmed to fans he will leave the club at the end of the season. "Given the ongoing uncertainty surrounding the club's ownership, the board believes it is right to manage the first team within our existing resources," a statement released by Eastleigh read. sports.title: Who is in the running for BBC Men's Footballer of the Year?
sports.description: [BBC] Voting has closed for the BBC Men's Footballer of the Year 2026 award, which will be presented at Sports Personality of the Year. Fans from the UK have been voting from the five-player shortlist of Jude Bellingham, Harry Kane, Kylian Mbappe, Rodri and Lamine Yamal. The winner of the award - new for this year - will be presented during the live Sports Personality of the Year show on Sunday, 13 December. "Our inaugural BBC Men's Footballer of the Year award is about recognising the players who have made this year so special, inspired fans and left their mark on the game. "It's a fantastic shortlist, and I can't wait to see who the public choose as our first-ever winner." The shortlist was selected by an expert panel comprising former international players and some of the BBC's most respected football voices, bringing together a wealth of experience and insight from across the game. The panel included Cesar Azpilicueta (Spain), Scott Brown (Scotland), Olivier Giroud (France), Shay Given (Republic of Ireland), Hassan Kachloul (Morocco), Lucas Leiva (Brazil), Benni McCarthy (South Africa), Alan Shearer, Ellen White (both England) and Ashley Williams (Wales). Read more on the five contenders below. sports.title: Why Cambridgeshire derby could be season-defining
sports.description: Robbie Savage's Peterborough United will seek to defend a long unbeaten home record in the Cambridgeshire derby when Neil Harris's U's visit London Road [Getty Images] History, tradition, bragging rights. Local derbies are always special, but none more so than when they have the ability to shape the narrative of a season. This much is true of Saturday's Cambridgeshire derby (12:30 GMT). Robbie Savage's Peterborough United welcome Neil Harris' Cambridge United to London Road with both at something of a crossroads. At stake for Posh? Their League One status. Despite an impressive win at Plymouth Argyle last time out, they remain 22nd in the table and need results to avoid a battle against the drop being the defining theme of their season. As for the U's, the derby presents an opportunity to regain momentum. After October's 2-1 win at Barnsley they were one point off top spot, but failure to pick up three points in any of their five league games since leaves them caught between play-off contention and mid-table drift. 'It's all about winning' The derby also carries the weight of recent history, with the emotional baggage greater for the U's. They have lost each of their past seven away league games against Peterborough, losing those matches by a combined 20-3 scoreline. Indeed, they have not won at London Road since an FA Cup tie in 1994-95, while their wait for a league win at their rivals' home extends to 1990. Savage, appointed last month, said his side were well aware of their responsibility for continuing that record. "We don't want to be the group that loses to Cambridge at home, first time in 30 years I think it would be," he said. "We don't want to be that group. We want to put three, four, five past them and win the game. Even if it's 1-0, it doesn't matter. "It's all about winning, don't care we win, just win the game." The victory at Plymouth ended a four-game wait for a win, and Savage said the onus was on his side to back it up on derby day. If they do, they know they will have secured successive league victories for the first time since February. "This game is at the top of the mountain," he said. "No doubt about it. sports.title: Gasly amused by Verstappen and Russell feud: 'I'm just eating my popcorn'
sports.description: Pierre Gasly has weighed in on the latest chapter of the bitter rivalry between Max Verstappen and George Russell , admitting that he is thoroughly enjoying watching the drama unfold from the sidelines. Tensions between Verstappen and Russell resurfaced during the Las Vegas Grand Prix weekend following an on-track altercation in the third and final free practice session, during which the pair made contact. The incident reignited a rivalry that reached boiling point at the end of the 2024 season in Qatar and Abu Dhabi, when the two drivers publicly traded accusations following a controversial qualifying incident in Lusail. Verstappen added further fuel to the fire following his victory in Las Vegas, claiming that Russell was "so far below my level" and remarking that "karma is a bi**h" following the Mercedes driver's difficult evening. Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Russell was subsequently given the opportunity to respond to the Dutchman's remarks ahead of this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix, describing the situation as unnecessary. The Mercedes driver stood by his criticism of Verstappen following their practice clash but insisted that he had no intention of prolonging their feud, acknowledging that he might have been too open when speaking to the media. Verstappen, meanwhile, refused to be drawn into another exchange of words with his rival during his media commitments in Qatar, insisting that everything that needed to be said off track had already been said. Gasly enjoys watching Verstappen and Russell's rivalry unfold The ongoing feud has also attracted the attention of several other drivers on the grid, including Gasly, who briefly partnered Verstappen at Red Bull in 2019 and has known both drivers since childhood. The Alpine driver admitted that he was enjoying the spectacle, suggesting that neither the altercation in Las Vegas nor the subsequent war of words came as a surprise to him: "Not the first time, not the last time these two are going to go at it. sports.title: Australia's sandpapergate probe to also include 2017-18 Ashes
sports.description: Australia won the 2017-18 Ashes series against England 4-0 [Getty Images] Cricket Australia's fresh independent probe into the sandpapergate scandal has been widened to include the 2017-18 Ashes series against England. The terms of reference for the independent forum have been published and the scope will include "ball-management practices in the Australian men's team during the 2017–18 season", which includes the Ashes series Australia won 4-0. Also included are all four Tests of the subsequent South Africa tour and the investigation which followed when the ball-tampering scandal emerged. Cricket Australia has pledged to publish the full independent report and recommendations within 30 days of receiving them. All those involved in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa will be invited to speak to the independent forum, though none will have to do so and no retrospective sanctions will be handed out. The scandal was reignited by the release of former batter Usman Khawaja's autobiography. In it, Khawaja claimed the entire team knew about ball-tampering in the third Test of their series against South Africa in Cape Town. The four frontline bowlers in that 2018 team - Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc, Nathan Lyon and current Test captain Pat Cummins - have always denied knowledge of the plan to use sandpaper on the ball. Cummins has called Khawaja's recollection of events "nonsense". However, former team-mates David Warner and Cameron Bancroft - two of three players who were banned for their part in the scandal, alongside Steve Smith - have backed Khawaja's version of events. "All participants in Australia's 2018 tour of South Africa, including players and support staff, will be invited to take part in the Independent Forum, as will CA management and directors at that time," Cricket Australia said. "While all involved will be encouraged to participate, there will be no compulsion to do so. All materials supplied will be treated as confidential unless otherwise stated by the participant and no sanctions will be retrospectively applied. "Participants can choose to attend the Independent Forum in person, online and/or provide information via written accounts or through relevant documents and materials." The forum will be open for six weeks. "This is an opportunity to provide their accounts in a safe environment and to provide the CA Board with relevant information including about the events of that tour and resultant investigation," CA chair David Boon said. "We are acutely aware of the enormous toll the renewed focus on this tour eight years ago has had on those involved and their welfare remains our main priority.
